input.title: Enable and fix React lint rules
input.task:
Repo: inkling (Electron + React + TypeScript + Vite, Bun, Windows app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root and follow it (performance principles, taste, verifying, comment rules enforced by `inkling/no-low-value-comments`, every `oxlint-disable` needs ` -- reason`). Do the work yourself; no subagents. Do NOT launch dev servers or the Electron app (the parent agent does the UI pass after you).

## Goal
`.oxlintrc.json` turns off several oxlint React rules that t3code (https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code) runs as errors: `react/refs`, `react/set-state-in-effect`, `react/exhaustive-effect-dependencies`, `react/immutability`; `react/purity` is not enabled. Fix the existing violations in `src/` and turn all five rules on as `error`, so effects that just sync state stop causing cascading renders and the lint holds the line.

## Known violations (measured on main with `bunx oxlint -D react/set-state-in-effect -D react/refs -D react/immutability -D react/exhaustive-effect-dependencies -D react/purity src`): ~25 diagnostics in 14 files: 13 set-state-in-effect, 8 refs, 2 immutability, 2 exhaustive-effect-dependencies, 0 purity. Files include src/components/mascot/InklingMascot.tsx, src/features/settings/useSettings.ts, src/features/settings/useArchive.ts, src/components/onboarding/SplitText.tsx, src/features/item-view/ZoomableImage.tsx, src/features/shell/useAppShortcuts.ts, src/App.tsx, src/features/item-view/PdfViewer.tsx, src/features/item-view/RichNoteEditor.tsx, src/features/shell/SpacesSection.tsx, src/components/ItemMedia.tsx, src/components/LiquidGlass.tsx, src/features/spaces/useSpaces.ts, src/components/FirstRunOverlay.tsx. Re-run the command yourself for the exact list.

## How to fix (behavior must not change)
- set-state-in-effect: derive the value during render, reset state with a `key`, or move the update into the event handler that causes it. If the effect truly synchronizes with something outside React and a synchronous setState is required (e.g. measuring layout, subscribing to a store/observer, a one-time mount read from an external API), keep it and add `// oxlint-disable-next-line react/set-state-in-effect -- <specific reason>`; the reason must say what external thing it syncs. Prefer a real fix; use disables sparingly and justify each.
- refs: do not read or write `ref.current` during render. Typical fixes: keep the latest-callback ref updates inside an effect or layout effect, or use state/derived value. Event handlers and effects may use refs.
- immutability (src/components/LiquidGlass.tsx ~line 433): do not mutate a value from useState or reassign locals after render.
- exhaustive-effect-dependencies: remove the extra dependencies, but double check the effect really should not re-run on them.
- Hot paths matter: the library grid, card, item overlay, and mascot are performance-sensitive. Do not add renders, re-subscriptions, or work per scroll/frame. No continuously repainting animations. Do not change the mascot's timing/behavior.
- Do not add comments restating code. Keep diffs small per file; no refactors beyond what each fix needs.
- Remove the `"off"` lines for these rules in `.oxlintrc.json` and set all five to `"error"` (`react/refs`, `react/set-state-in-effect`, `react/exhaustive-effect-dependencies`, `react/immutability`, `react/purity`). Leave other rules as they are. Check the overrides section still makes sense.

## Proof
- `bunx oxlint src` and `bunx oxlint` (whole repo lint, fast) clean with the new config; `bunx oxfmt --check` on files you changed; `bun run typecheck`; `bun test` only for test files beside the files you changed (a test covering a hook you altered must pass). No full `bun test` sweep.
- If a fix changes logic that has no test and is easy to break quietly (ordering/race of state), add one focused test per AGENTS.md test rules; otherwise do not add tests.
- In the PR body list each file and the kind of fix, and call out every `oxlint-disable` you kept with its reason, so the parent can do a targeted UI pass on those areas.
- docs/changelog.md: skip unless a user-visible behavior changed (it should not).

## Delivery (full-stop: PR ready for the user, never merged by you)
- Branch from latest origin/main (`git fetch origin; git switch -c fix/react-lint-rules origin/main`).
- Conventional commit, e.g. `fix(react): stop syncing state in effects and enable the React lint rules`. End with your own `Co-Authored-By: <your model name> <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Push and open a PR with `gh` (use the `file-pr` skill if you have it). Body: problem in a sentence or two, how fixed, one line on proof, the per-file list above; end with your model name and harness `(T3 Code)`, then `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- Never merge, enable auto-merge, or call watch_pull_request; no sleeping or polling; look at check state once.
- Last line of your final message exactly: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`. Above it, 4-8 lines: what you fixed, which disables remain, which fixes are riskiest for a UI pass.

- refs: do not read or write `ref.current` during render. Typical fixes: keep the latest-callback ref updates inside an effect or layout effect, or use state/derived value. Event handlers and effects may use refs.
- immutability (src/components/LiquidGlass.tsx ~line 433): do not mutate a value from useState or reassign locals after render.
- exhaustive-effect-dependencies: remove the extra dependencies, but double check the effect really should not re-run on them.
- Hot paths matter: the library grid, card, item overlay, and mascot are performance-sensitive. Do not add renders, re-subscriptions, or work per scroll/frame. No continuously repainting animations. Do not change the mascot's timing/behavior.
- Do not add comments restating code. Keep diffs small per file; no refactors beyond what each fix needs.

## Proof

input.title: Add bun run check:changed
input.task:
Repo: inkling (Electron + React + TS, Bun, Windows app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root and follow it (verifying rules, docs rules, PR rules, the "three ways to hurt yourself"). Do the work yourself; no subagents. This machine is Windows; use Bun APIs with argument arrays, no shell string commands, and no bash-only syntax in the script.

## Goal
Add `bun run check:changed`: one command an agent or dev runs while iterating and before pushing. It runs the fast subset of CI's checks for only what the branch changed. `bun run check` (the full CI mirror) stays as is. Inspiration is t3code's `scripts/check-changed.ts` (https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/main/scripts/check-changed.ts), but ours must be much smaller: yagni, aim for roughly 100 lines. Do NOT copy its run-result cache, workspace/affected-package mapping, patch check, or GraphQL parts.

## Behavior
- `bun run check:changed` compares against `git merge-base HEAD origin/main`; optional first argument is another ref. If there is no merge base, print a one-line hint to `git fetch origin` and exit 1.
- Changed files = `git diff --name-only --no-renames <base>` plus untracked files (`git ls-files --others --exclude-standard`). Only files that still exist are passed to tools. No changes -> print so and exit 0.
- Steps (run concurrently, print each step's output when it finishes, then a pass/fail summary, exit non-zero if any failed):
  1. `oxlint` on changed JS/TS files (`bunx oxlint <files>` or the local binary; match how package.json's `lint` script invokes it).
  2. `oxfmt --check` on changed files oxfmt handles. Make sure files in `.oxfmtrc.json` ignorePatterns (md, yml, bun.lock, etc.) are not passed in a way that makes oxfmt error with "no target files"; test this with a docs-only change and with an ignored file.
  3. `bun test` on changed test files plus sibling tests of changed source files (`foo.ts` -> `foo.test.ts` in the same directory; also `.test.tsx`). Skip the step when none.
  4. `bun run knip` when any code file or package.json/knip.json changed.
  5. `bun run typecheck` when any code or tsconfig/package.json changed (it is fast enough to run whole).
- Must work on Windows (backslash paths from git are forward-slash; normalize anyway) and in a git worktree.

## Also update (same change)
- `package.json`: add the `check:changed` script.
- `t3.json`: add a matching run script entry (AGENTS.md requires t3.json to stay in sync with package.json scripts).
- `AGENTS.md` "Verifying": the first bullet currently hand-composes `bun test <files>`, `bunx oxlint <files>`, `bunx oxfmt --check <files>`, `bun run typecheck`. Replace that with `bun run check:changed` as the pre-push command (keep `bun test <files>` for fast iteration and keep the "do not run repo-wide checks" rule and the note that `bun run check` mirrors CI). Edit only that bullet; do not touch "Where code lives" or "How it works" (other open PRs edit those).
- `docs/operations/development.md`: add it where the commands/checks are listed. Keep it to a line or two.
- `bun run check:refs` must pass (it validates command references in docs).
- Skip the changelog (internal dev tooling, trivial per docs rules) unless docs/changelog.md's header says otherwise.
- A test only if the file-to-test mapping has non-obvious logic; do not add trivial tests. Prove it works by running `bun run check:changed` on your own branch's changes, on a docs-only change, on an empty diff, and once with a deliberately broken lint/test change (revert it afterwards). Report the observed results.

## Delivery (full-stop: PR ready for the user, never merged by you)
- Branch from latest origin/main (`git fetch origin; git switch -c chore/check-changed origin/main`). Other PRs are open, so keep the diff to the files above.
- Conventional commit, e.g. `chore(scripts): add check:changed for fast pre-push checks`. End the commit message with your own `Co-Authored-By: <your model name> <noreply@anthropic.com>` line.
- Push and open a PR with `gh` (use the `file-pr` skill if you have it). Body: the problem in a sentence or two (agents hand-assemble checks), how you fixed it, one line on how you verified, and end with your model name and harness `(T3 Code)`, then `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- Never merge, enable auto-merge, or push to main. Do not call watch_pull_request; do not poll or sleep. Look at check state once.
- Last line of your final message exactly: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`. Above it, 3-6 lines on what you did and any doubts.

input.title: Move frontend CI to Windows
input.task:
Repo: inkling (Electron + React + TS, Bun, Windows-only desktop app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root and follow it. Do the work yourself; no subagents. This machine is Windows, which is the same OS CI will use, so reproduce locally instead of burning CI runs.

## Goal
The `frontend` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on `ubuntu-24.04`, so `bun test` (including asset path containment in `electron/storage/shared.ts` `isInside`, which depends on `node:path` separators) only proves POSIX behavior while the app ships on Windows. Move the `frontend` job to `windows-latest` so the full suite runs on the real target OS. (t3code has a Windows test lane in `.github/workflows/windows-tests.yml`; ours runs by default instead of on manual dispatch because our app is Windows-only.)

## Requirements
- Keep the `changes` (path filter) job on ubuntu. Move only `frontend` to `windows-latest`. Keep the job name `Frontend checks` and job id `frontend` unchanged (branch protection may require that name). Do not touch the Linux Xvfb smoke job in `electron-preview.yml` or release workflows.
- Windows runner shell gotcha: the default shell is pwsh, and in a multi-line `run: |` block a failing native command in the middle does NOT fail the step; only the last command's exit code counts. Steps with several commands (the typecheck workspaces step, the canary step) must either use `shell: bash` (GitHub's bash step uses `set -e` semantics) or be split into one command per step. Pick the smallest approach and apply it to every multi-command step.
- Line endings: Windows runners may check out with CRLF, which can make `oxfmt --check` or tests fail. Check `.gitattributes` and the checkout config; make the checkout produce LF the way the repo expects (e.g. a `.gitattributes` eol rule or `git config --global core.autocrlf false` before checkout) if needed. Keep this minimal and only if the evidence shows it is needed.
- Fix any test that fails on Windows. Locally run the full CI frontend sequence once on this machine (this task explicitly authorizes a full `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run knip`, `bun run lint`, `bun run build`, `bun run build:app`, `bun run ingest:smoke`; skip steps that are clearly the same on every OS if slow, but do run `bun test`). Also run the typecheck/canary commands as CI does. Fix real failures with the smallest change; if a failure is a genuine Windows-only product bug rather than a test assumption, report it instead of papering over it.
- Update docs that describe CI: `docs/operations/development.md` (CI behavior section) and CONTRIBUTING.md if they say CI runs on Linux. Rewrite the affected sentence; do not append.
- `ci.yml` is not covered by CI's paths-ignore, so CI will run on your PR with the real result. That run is your final proof.

## Delivery (full-send, but YOU do not merge or watch; the parent agent will)
- Branch from latest origin/main (`git fetch origin; git switch -c ci/frontend-on-windows origin/main`). Note #194 recently changed ci.yml, so start from fresh main.
- Conventional commit, e.g. `ci(github): run the frontend checks on windows-latest`. End with your own `Co-Authored-By: <your model name> <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Push and open a PR with `gh` (use the `file-pr` skill if you have it). Body: problem in a sentence or two, what changed, one line on proof (local Windows run results + note CI result), end with your model name and harness `(T3 Code)`, then `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)`.
- Do not merge, enable auto-merge, or call watch_pull_request. No sleeping or polling; look at check state once after pushing and report it.
- Last line of your final message exactly: `PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>`. Above it, 3-8 lines: what you changed, what failed on Windows and how you fixed it, local run timings if useful, doubts.

input.title: Enable and fix React lint rules
input.task:
Repo: inkling (Electron + React + TypeScript + Vite, Bun, Windows app). Read AGENTS.md at the repo root and follow it (performance principles, taste, verifying, comment rules enforced by `inkling/no-low-value-comments`, every `oxlint-disable` needs ` -- reason`). ## Goal
`.oxlintrc.json` turns off several oxlint React rules that t3code (https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code) runs as errors: `react/refs`, `react/set-state-in-effect`, `react/exhaustive-effect-dependencies`, `react/immutability`; `react/purity` is not enabled. Fix the existing violations in `src/` and turn all five rules on as `error`, so effects that just sync state stop causing cascading renders and the lint holds the line.

## Known violations (measured on main with `bunx oxlint -D react/set-state-in-effect -D react/refs -D react/immutability -D react/exhaustive-effect-dependencies -D react/purity src`): ~25 diagnostics in 14 files: 13 set-state-in-effect, 8 refs, 2 immutability, 2 exhaustive-effect-dependencies, 0 purity. Files include src/components/mascot/InklingMascot.tsx, src/features/settings/useSettings.ts, src/features/settings/useArchive.ts, src/components/onboarding/SplitText.tsx, src/features/item-view/ZoomableImage.tsx, src/features/shell/useAppShortcuts.ts, src/App.tsx, src/features/item-view/PdfViewer.tsx, src/features/item-view/RichNoteEditor.tsx, src/features/shell/SpacesSection.tsx, src/components/ItemMedia.tsx, src/components/LiquidGlass.tsx, src/features/spaces/useSpaces.ts, src/components/FirstRunOverlay.tsx. Re-run the command yourself for the exact list.

## How to fix (behavior must not change)
- set-state-in-effect: derive the value during render, reset state with a `key`, or move the update into the event handler that causes it. If the effect truly synchronizes with something outside React and a synchronous setState is required (e.g. measuring layout, subscribing to a store/observer, a one-time mount read from an external API), keep it and add `// oxlint-disable-next-line react/set-state-in-effect -- <specific reason>`; the reason must say what external thing it syncs. Prefer a real fix; use disables sparingly and justify each.
- refs: do not read or write `ref.current` during render. Typical fixes: keep the latest-callback ref updates inside an effect or layout effect, or use state/derived value. Event handlers and effects may use refs.

content.content: {"host":"github.com","repository":"squidys-tools/inkling","number":196,"url":"https://github.com/Squidys-Tools/inkling/pull/196","watching":true,"wasWatching":false}

1	---
2	name: verify-inkling
3	description: Drive the inkling Electron desktop app as a user would and prove a feature works. Use when a change touches capture, search, Spaces, note editing, archive or restore, or any user-visible behavior, and you need launch, doctor, drive, evidence, and cleanup on Windows or Linux (Linux runs under Xvfb). Uses CDP against an isolated scratch library; never the real user library.
4	---
5	
6	# verify-inkling
7	
8	Proves inkling behavior by driving the real Electron app over Chrome DevTools Protocol against a scratch data dir. The feature map lives in `features/`; start at `features/README.md` and drive one feature per run.
9	
10	## Rules
11	
12	- Use only the scratch library under `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` (override the parent with `INKLING_VERIFY_DIR`). Never point at the developer's real library, never copy from it.
13	- Stop only the pid this run recorded in `electron.pid` after confirming its cmdline. Never `pkill`, never match processes by name.
14	- Run one integrated pass per change. Do not run the full suite; CI owns it.
15	- Linux cannot verify Windows-only behavior (OCR through Windows.Media, WebView2). Report those as unverified.
16	- Drive through the UI handles below, not internal setters or test-only endpoints.
17	
18	## Setup
19	
20	Use the bun version in `.bun-version`; `bun run check:bun-version` says if it is wrong.
21	
22	```sh
23	bun install
24	bun run build:app      # produces dist/; prints "No demo seed in N built files"
25	```
26	
27	## Launch
28	
29	Same commands on Windows and Linux. Launch starts Electron detached and returns once the app page is listed:
30	
31	```sh
32	bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch
33	```
34	
35	It runs `node_modules/electron/dist/electron .` with `--remote-debugging-port=9333 --user-data-dir=<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/default/library`, writing `electron.pid` and `electron.log` beside the library. On Linux with no `DISPLAY` it wraps Electron in `xvfb-run -a` and adds `--no-sandbox`. Ready means `app://local/index.html` is listed at `http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list`, which takes about 10 seconds. The first launch against an empty dir shows "0 items in library".
36	
37	Two instances side by side: give each its own name and port, `INKLING_VERIFY_NAME=b INKLING_VERIFY_PORT=9334 bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch`, then pass the same two variables to doctor, drive, and cleanup.
38	
39	## Doctor
40	
41	Read-only. Run it first whenever anything looks off:
42	
43	```sh
44	bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs doctor
45	```
46	
47	Every line must read PASS and the exit code must be 0: pidfile present, pid alive, pid runs our scratch dir, CDP port owned by that pid, app page loaded, library database exists, renderer build present.
48	
49	## Drive
50	
51	`scripts/drive.mjs` runs an ordered list of steps against the page and writes evidence. Steps are JSON objects with one key each:
52	
53	- `click`: CSS selector, clicks the first match.
54	- `clickText`: `{selector, text}`, clicks the first match whose text contains `text`.
55	- `fill`: CSS selector plus `text`, focuses and inserts text.
56	- `key`: `Enter`, `Escape`, or a single character.
57	- `wait`: selector that must appear.
58	- `expect`: JavaScript expression that must become true.
59	- `shot`: PNG filename written into the evidence dir.
60	
61	Each step may set `label`, and `timeoutMs` (default 8000). A failed step writes `failure.png` and stops the run.
62	
63	```sh
64	bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/drive.mjs 9333 <steps.json> .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>
65	```
66	
67	Selectors come from `src/App.tsx` and `src/features/item-view/`. Prefer the aria-label, title, and class names listed in each feature file over coordinates. Only `features/capture-note.md` has a proven step list; the other feature files are mapped but not yet driven.
68	
69	## Evidence
70	
71	Every run writes to `.artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` (gitignored):
72	
73	- `steps.log`: one PASS or FAIL line per step.
74	- `console.log`: renderer console, exceptions, and log entries captured during the run.
75	- Numbered screenshots from `shot` steps, plus `failure.png` on a failed step.
76	- Database proof: read the scratch `library.sqlite3` with bun's `bun:sqlite` in readonly mode, for example `items` rows with `kind`, `body`, `archived`. Include the query output in the run notes.
77	
78	A proof must show the user action, the visible result, and the stored side effect. A card on screen with no row in `items` is not a pass, and neither is a row with no card.
79	
80	## Cleanup
81	
82	Run this after every run, including failed ones:
83	
84	```sh
85	bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs cleanup

---
name: verify-inkling
description: Drive the inkling Electron desktop app as a user would and prove a feature works. Use when a change touches capture, search, Spaces, note editing, archive or restore, or any user-visible behavior, and you need launch, doctor, drive, evidence, and cleanup on Windows or Linux (Linux runs under Xvfb). Uses CDP against an isolated scratch library; never the real user library.
---

# verify-inkling

Proves inkling behavior by driving the real Electron app over Chrome DevTools Protocol against a scratch data dir. The feature map lives in `features/`; start at `features/README.md` and drive one feature per run.

## Rules

- Use only the scratch library under `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` (override the parent with `INKLING_VERIFY_DIR`). Never point at the developer's real library, never copy from it.
- Stop only the pid this run recorded in `electron.pid` after confirming its cmdline. Never `pkill`, never match processes by name.
- Run one integrated pass per change. Do not run the full suite; CI owns it.
- Linux cannot verify Windows-only behavior (OCR through Windows.Media, WebView2). Report those as unverified.
- Drive through the UI handles below, not internal setters or test-only endpoints.

## Setup

Use the bun version in `.bun-version`; `bun run check:bun-version` says if it is wrong.

```sh
bun install
bun run build:app      # produces dist/; prints "No demo seed in N built files"
```

## Launch

Same commands on Windows and Linux. Launch starts Electron detached and returns once the app page is listed:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch
```

It runs `node_modules/electron/dist/electron .` with `--remote-debugging-port=9333 --user-data-dir=<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/default/library`, writing `electron.pid` and `electron.log` beside the library. On Linux with no `DISPLAY` it wraps Electron in `xvfb-run -a` and adds `--no-sandbox`. Ready means `app://local/index.html` is listed at `http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list`, which takes about 10 seconds. The first launch against an empty dir shows "0 items in library".

Two instances side by side: give each its own name and port, `INKLING_VERIFY_NAME=b INKLING_VERIFY_PORT=9334 bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch`, then pass the same two variables to doctor, drive, and cleanup.

## Doctor

Read-only. Run it first whenever anything looks off:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs doctor
```

Every line must read PASS and the exit code must be 0: pidfile present, pid alive, pid runs our scratch dir, CDP port owned by that pid, app page loaded, library database exists, renderer build present.

## Drive

`scripts/drive.mjs` runs an ordered list of steps against the page and writes evidence. Steps are JSON objects with one key each:

- `click`: CSS selector, clicks the first match.
- `clickText`: `{selector, text}`, clicks the first match whose text contains `text`.
- `fill`: CSS selector plus `text`, focuses and inserts text.
- `key`: `Enter`, `Escape`, or a single character.
- `wait`: selector that must appear.
- `expect`: JavaScript expression that must become true.
- `shot`: PNG filename written into the evidence dir.

Each step may set `label`, and `timeoutMs` (default 8000). A failed step writes `failure.png` and stops the run.

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/drive.mjs 9333 <steps.json> .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>
```

Selectors come from `src/App.tsx` and `src/features/item-view/`. Prefer the aria-label, title, and class names listed in each feature file over coordinates. Only `features/capture-note.md` has a proven step list; the other feature files are mapped but not yet driven.

## Evidence

Every run writes to `.artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` (gitignored):

- `steps.log`: one PASS or FAIL line per step.
- `console.log`: renderer console, exceptions, and log entries captured during the run.
- Numbered screenshots from `shot` steps, plus `failure.png` on a failed step.
- Database proof: read the scratch `library.sqlite3` with bun's `bun:sqlite` in readonly mode, for example `items` rows with `kind`, `body`, `archived`. Include the query output in the run notes.

A proof must show the user action, the visible result, and the stored side effect. A card on screen with no row in `items` is not a pass, and neither is a row with no card.

## Cleanup

Run this after every run, including failed ones:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs cleanup
```

It stops only the recorded pid, then removes that instance's scratch library and pidfile. It confirms the pid's command line names the scratch library first, so a recycled pid is never touched. It never touches `.artifacts/`. Confirm afterwards with `ls .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` that the evidence survived, and that `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` is gone.

## Known platform noise

On Linux, Xvfb has no dbus session, so dbus and dconf errors in `electron.log` are environment noise, not app errors. The sharp Linux warning is also environment-only. Packaged Linux PDF.js worker failure is pre-existing and not caused by this skill.

## Keeping the map current

When a feature's selectors or flow change, update its file in `features/`. `/maintain-verification-skill` is the maintenance loop for keeping this map honest.

# Capture a note from the Add menu

## Sub-features

- Note tile in the Add menu.
- Save to library button; the card appears before any processing finishes.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click Add at the foot of the sidebar. It opens into a menu of Note, Link, Quote, File, and Screen (screenshot). Choose Note, type a line, and press Enter or Save to library. The new card lands at the top of Everything.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Save as `steps.json`, then run with a fresh evidence dir:

```json
[
  {"label": "open Add", "click": "button[data-tooltip='Add something to your library']"},
  {"label": "choose Note", "clickText": {"selector": ".add-menu-tile", "text": "Note"}},
  {"label": "note field", "wait": "textarea[aria-label='New note']"},
  {"label": "type note", "fill": "textarea[aria-label='New note']", "text": "verify-inkling probe note"},
  {"label": "save", "click": "button.add-menu-save"},
  {"label": "card shows", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('verify-inkling probe note'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "shot", "shot": "note-saved.png"}
]
```

End state proof: the card with the text is in the grid, and `items` has one row with `kind = 'note'`, `body = 'verify-inkling probe note'`, `body_format = 'md'`, `archived = 0`. The title stays null for notes.

## Gotchas

- Note title is null; the text lives in `body`. Check `body`, not `title`.
- The menu only appears on Add, which lives in the sidebar. Opening Add another way (the N shortcut) opens the sidebar too.
- Link, File, Quote, and Screenshot are not driven by this map yet.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion

  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).

    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

|---|---|
| New-Space input focus | focused on open; Regular Space created, stored as `regular` in the DB |

# inkling

inkling is a home for everything worth keeping. Articles, images, screenshots, PDFs, notes, quotes, video links. An Electron desktop app for Windows, with React, TypeScript, and Vite in the frontend and Node.js and SQLite in the backend. Everything stays on the machine.

Think of it as a private visual library with semantic search as the only organizer. No folders to maintain. Save arbitrary media in seconds, find it later by describing it.

## What makes inkling special

People keep things here they do not want to lose, things that are important to them, or that give them inspiration or creative ideas. These are the things that we must never compromise on.

### 1. Capture is instant and seamless

Saving must be faster than deciding where something belongs. The card appears right away. OCR, embeddings, fetching and/or indexing run in the background while the user keeps browsing or continues on with something else. A change that blocks capture on processing is a bug, no matter how correct the processing is.

### 2. Performance

Lots of apps have gotten bogged down with bad tech decisions and "slop". We regularly audit for performance regressions, often caused by passing full content over Electron IPC instead of summaries/thumbnails, rendering the card grid without virtualization, loading full assets where a thumbnail would do, blocking capture on extraction/OCR/embeddings, and running FTS + vector + Smart Space re-evaluation on every keystroke. - Before finishing: link the PR to the issue at the top of the description before all content, move it to In Review, tick the `roadmap.md` box and add a changelog line referencing the issue ID in the same PR.
- If merged: move the issue to Done.

## Documentation

Most code changes need no docs change. Agents can read the code.

- Product intent lives in `docs/product.md` and `docs/product-behavior.md`. Architecture reasons live in `docs/tech-stack.md`. Standing goes in `docs/roadmap.md`. What changed goes in `docs/changelog.md`. Do not invent a second place for the same fact.
- Before adding a paragraph, ask what a maintainer would get wrong without it. If reading the relevant code answers the question, leave it out.
- Do not document every feature, enumerate fields or methods, narrate control flow, maintain file catalogs, or append PR summaries. Types, tests, and code already record the implementation. The glossary defines shared vocabulary; it is not a feature index.
- Keep a local implementation explanation in a nearby code comment. Use an internal doc when the reasoning crosses boundaries or needs context the code cannot carry well. Link to the relevant source instead of copying it.
- When a documented decision or constraint changes, rewrite or remove the affected text. Do not append another account of the new behavior. A new internal page needs a distinct, durable reason to exist.
- Keep user docs in the shipped product's voice, without implementation details or contributor tooling. Update the relevant feature section when how to use it changes. A UI tweak does not need a documentation entry, and a new control does not need its own page. A settings path is useful; descriptions of visible buttons, icons, layouts, animations, or every UI state are not. Before adding text, ask what task or decision it helps the user with.
- The changelog rules live at the top of `docs/changelog.md` and still apply. One line per entry, grouped under Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed, Deprecated, Security. Trivial edits skip the changelog.
- `docs/operations/` holds maintainer setup, release, and debugging procedures. Keep instructions for operating an installed inkling version in the user guides.

## Plans and work artifacts

- Do not commit implementation plans, research notes, or agent scratch files. Keep temporary working material outside the worktree. `.plans/` is gitignored only as a safety net for legacy tooling.
- Track active maintainer work in its Linear issue (see [Linear issues](#linear-issues)). External proposals follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
- A merged PR is the implementation record. Do not keep a task checklist in the repository; `docs/roadmap.md` records milestone standing only.

## How it works

Capture creates the item immediately, then background jobs do the slow parts. Normalize, extract text and metadata, run OCR or PDF extraction or article parsing, generate embeddings. Writes to items update the FTS index through triggers. The user keeps browsing or does something else while jobs run. A job can be retried, its lease can expire, and interrupted jobs recover on restart.

Search combines exact FTS over content, notes, and OCR text with semantic similarity over local embeddings. Smart Spaces are saved searches whose query runs each time their items load, so they need no background job.

The Electron main process owns files, the job queue, the database, and model execution. The renderer gets a narrow preload bridge, not raw filesystem or shell access. Fetched HTML is untrusted. It gets sanitized, embeds pass an allowlist, scripts and event handlers are stripped.

Full reasoning in `docs/tech-stack.md`. Behavior contract in `docs/product-behavior.md`.

## Where code lives

- `src/` is the React and TypeScript frontend. Entry at `src/main.tsx`.
- `src/lib/ingestion/` is the capture and extraction pipeline. Defuddle, metadata fallback, sanitizing, video link handling.
- `src/components/` holds shared pieces such as the card media (`ItemMedia.tsx`), the expanded item overlay, and the PDF viewer. The library grid, cards, and Spaces UI live in `src/App.tsx`, and the reader is `src/ReaderView.tsx`.
- `electron/` holds the desktop main process, preload bridge, SQLite storage, job queue, PDF/OCR, embeddings, and packaging inputs.
- `benchmarks/` holds the corpus, the harness, expected outputs, and results. Of the results, only `results-latest.json` and `summary.md` are tracked.
- `public/seed-demo/` plus `src/seedPersonal.ts` is the committed demo library for UI work.

## Taste

- Complexity belongs at the adapter boundary. Ingestion stays explicit, UI stays dumb.
- Inferred types over annotations. `any` is the enemy.
- Effect lives in the main process and stops at the IPC edge. The one renderer use is `src/lib/ingestion/http.ts` (preview-mode capture); don't add more. Reusable Effect functions use `Effect.fnUntraced`, not `Effect.fn` (nothing collects spans). Keep `Effect.gen` for inline programs and layers.
- Default to no comment. Keep one only where a reader would likely break something without it: a race or ordering guarantee, a security or sanitizing check, a Chromium, Electron, WebGPU or OS quirk, or an invariant another file relies on. One line where you can, four at most. Don't restate names, narrate steps, label sections, record history, explain the fix you just made (the PR carries that), or leave a TODO without an issue. Lint directives, knip tags and license headers stay. `inkling/no-low-value-comments` in `oxlint-plugin-inkling/` enforces the length cap and the mechanical cases, and every `oxlint-disable` needs a `-- reason`.
- Our users should never notice a dropped frame, a lying spinner, and a stale label. No continuously repainting animations (with a slight exception for the mascot); they peg the GPU on high-refresh displays.
- Capture paths stay fast and forgiving. Keep partial results when extraction fails. A URL with a title and domain beats an error card.

## Additional tips

- Security is important, but should not be over-indexed on, especially for dev mode/maintainer-only features. The main threat is untrusted web content rendered locally; `docs/tech-stack.md` says to treat all fetched HTML as untrusted. Keep sanitizing and allowlists strict. Keep dev ergonomics simple.

# Capture a note from the Add menu

## Sub-features

- Note tile in the Add menu.
- Save to library button; the card appears before any processing finishes.

## How to get to it (user POV)

Click Add at the foot of the sidebar. It opens into a menu of Note, Link, Quote, File, and Screen (screenshot). Choose Note, type a line, and press Enter or Save to library. The new card lands at the top of Everything.

## Driving it with `scripts/drive.mjs`

Save as `steps.json`, then run with a fresh evidence dir:

```json
[
  {"label": "open Add", "click": "button[data-tooltip='Add something to your library']"},
  {"label": "choose Note", "clickText": {"selector": ".add-menu-tile", "text": "Note"}},
  {"label": "note field", "wait": "textarea[aria-label='New note']"},
  {"label": "type note", "fill": "textarea[aria-label='New note']", "text": "verify-inkling probe note"},
  {"label": "save", "click": "button.add-menu-save"},
  {"label": "card shows", "expect": "[...document.querySelectorAll('article')].some(a => a.textContent.includes('verify-inkling probe note'))", "timeoutMs": 10000},
  {"label": "shot", "shot": "note-saved.png"}
]
```

End state proof: the card with the text is in the grid, and `items` has one row with `kind = 'note'`, `body = 'verify-inkling probe note'`, `body_format = 'md'`, `archived = 0`. The title stays null for notes.

- Note title is null; the text lives in `body`. Check `body`, not `title`.
- The menu only appears on Add, which lives in the sidebar. Opening Add another way (the N shortcut) opens the sidebar too.
- Link, File, Quote, and Screenshot are not driven by this map yet.

---
name: verify-inkling
description: Drive the inkling Electron desktop app as a user would and prove a feature works. Use when a change touches capture, search, Spaces, note editing, archive or restore, or any user-visible behavior, and you need launch, doctor, drive, evidence, and cleanup on Windows or Linux (Linux runs under Xvfb). Uses CDP against an isolated scratch library; never the real user library.
---

# verify-inkling

Proves inkling behavior by driving the real Electron app over Chrome DevTools Protocol against a scratch data dir. The feature map lives in `features/`; start at `features/README.md` and drive one feature per run.

## Rules

- Use only the scratch library under `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` (override the parent with `INKLING_VERIFY_DIR`). Never point at the developer's real library, never copy from it.
- Stop only the pid this run recorded in `electron.pid` after confirming its cmdline. Never `pkill`, never match processes by name.
- Run one integrated pass per change. Do not run the full suite; CI owns it.
- Linux cannot verify Windows-only behavior (OCR through Windows.Media, WebView2). Report those as unverified.
- Drive through the UI handles below, not internal setters or test-only endpoints.

## Setup

Use the Bun version in `.bun-version`; `bun run check:bun-version` says if it is wrong.

```sh
bun install
bun run build:app      # produces dist/; prints "No demo seed in N built files"
```

## Launch

Same commands on Windows and Linux. Launch starts Electron detached and returns once the app page is listed:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch
```

It runs `node_modules/electron/dist/electron .` with `--remote-debugging-port=9333 --user-data-dir=<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/default/library`, writing `electron.pid` and `electron.log` beside the library. On Linux with no `DISPLAY` it wraps Electron in `xvfb-run -a` and adds `--no-sandbox`. Ready means `app://local/index.html` is listed at `http://127.0.0.1:9333/json/list`, which takes about 10 seconds. The first launch against an empty dir shows "0 items in library".

Two instances side by side: give each its own name and port, `INKLING_VERIFY_NAME=b INKLING_VERIFY_PORT=9334 bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs launch`, then pass the same two variables to doctor, drive, and cleanup.

## Doctor

Read-only. Run it first whenever anything looks off:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs doctor
```

Every line must read PASS and the exit code must be 0: pidfile present, pid alive, pid runs our scratch dir, CDP port owned by that pid, app page loaded, library database exists, renderer build present.

## Drive

`scripts/drive.mjs` runs an ordered list of steps against the page and writes evidence. Steps are JSON objects with one key each:

- `click`: CSS selector, clicks the first match.
- `clickText`: `{selector, text}`, clicks the first match whose text contains `text`.
- `fill`: CSS selector plus `text`, focuses and inserts text.
- `key`: `Enter`, `Escape`, or a single character.
- `wait`: selector that must appear.
- `expect`: JavaScript expression that must become true.
- `shot`: PNG filename written into the evidence dir.

Each step may set `label`, and `timeoutMs` (default 8000). A failed step writes `failure.png` and stops the run.

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/drive.mjs 9333 <steps.json> .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>
```

Selectors come from `src/App.tsx` and `src/features/item-view/`. Prefer the aria-label, title, and class names listed in each feature file over coordinates. Only `features/capture-note.md` has a proven step list; the other feature files are mapped but not yet driven.

## Evidence

Every run writes to `.artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` (gitignored):

- `steps.log`: one PASS or FAIL line per step.
- `console.log`: renderer console, exceptions, and log entries captured during the run.
- Numbered screenshots from `shot` steps, plus `failure.png` on a failed step.
- Database proof: read the scratch `library.sqlite3` with bun's `bun:sqlite` in readonly mode, for example `items` rows with `kind`, `body`, `archived`. Include the query output in the run notes.

A proof must show the user action, the visible result, and the stored side effect. A card on screen with no row in `items` is not a pass, and neither is a row with no card.

## Cleanup

Run this after every run, including failed ones:

```sh
bun .claude/skills/verify-inkling/scripts/instance.mjs cleanup
```

It stops only the recorded pid, then removes that instance's scratch library and pidfile. It confirms the pid's command line names the scratch library first, so a recycled pid is never touched. It never touches `.artifacts/`. Confirm afterwards with `ls .artifacts/verify-inkling/<run-name>/` that the evidence survived, and that `<tmpdir>/verify-inkling-run/<NAME>/library` is gone.

## Known platform noise

On Linux, Xvfb has no dbus session, so dbus and dconf errors in `electron.log` are environment noise, not app errors. The sharp Linux warning is also environment-only. Packaged Linux PDF.js worker failure is pre-existing and not caused by this skill.

## Keeping the map current

When a feature's selectors or flow change, update its file in `features/`. `/maintain-verification-skill` is the maintenance loop for keeping this map honest.

# Full Send

If the user triggered this, it's because they are not watching this thread, and
they want you to complete the work end-to-end autonomously. Your updates and
your final message go unread until long after you stop. You own the work from
its current state to a merged PR.

If the user did not explicitly request "full send" in some clear way, do not
assume full autonomy. If they did, everything below applies.

The user grants you permission to:

- Merge the PR once the merge gate passes.
- Force-push the PR's own branch with `--force-with-lease` after a rebase.
- Use the test methods that Proof needs, without asking first.

## Testing permission

A "full send" request is the permission. If a project file or other
instruction says to ask before a test method, or to leave testing to the
user, this request replaces that rule for this task.

That includes ask-first rules for computer use, browser automation,
simulators and devices, running the app or a dev server, screenshots, and
visual checks. Use the method that gives direct proof. List it in the
report.

Rules about how to test still apply. Follow rules that name the correct
command, fixture, or check. This permission only removes the ask-first or
leave-it-to-the-user step. If a preferred method cannot prove the change,
use a gated method under this permission.

It covers only the tests needed for this task. It does not add permission
for the steps under "Asking the user", such as production changes or data
deletion. It also does not bypass a harness or system approval prompt if
one appears.

## Steps

1. **Finish the change.** Complete the goal from the user's request with the
   smallest change that works. Fix the case that happened, not every case
   that could. If you are on the default branch, create a branch first.
2. **Prove it.** Get proof for every change you made. See "Proof".
3. **Get feedback.** Use the `smol-loop` skill to verify changes.
4. **File the PR** with the `file-pr` skill. Rebase onto the latest default
   branch first. Add one short line to the description that says how you proved
   the change.
5. **Babysit the PR** with the `babysit-pr` skill. Fix real findings and CI
   failures. Get proof for each fix before you push it.
6. **Merge** when the merge gate passes.
7. **Report** in your final message: the PR link, the merge commit, your proof,
   and each decision you made for the user.

Stay active from step 1 to step 7. If you end your turn while checks or bots are
pending, the work stops, because nobody will prompt you again. Wait with the
watcher from `babysit-pr`, so something wakes you when the PR changes. In T3
Code that is `watch_pull_request`. If you stop before the merge, call
`unwatch_pull_request` first.

## Proof

Proof is evidence you observed yourself in this session: command output, a
reproduction, a screenshot. Use the most direct proof the change allows:

- Reproduce the original failure, apply the fix, then watch the same
  reproduction pass.
- Run the checks that the repo's CI runs (typecheck, lint, tests).
- Add one focused test that fails without the fix, when the behavior has none
  and the repo has a test setup.
- For UI and runtime behavior, run the app and look at the change. Green mocked
  tests do not prove that the user experience works. Attach screenshots to the
  PR when they help and you have a way to upload them.

When you cannot find a way to prove a change, you do not have full confidence.
Ask the user.

## Merge gate

Full confidence means all of these are true on the latest commit:

- Your proof covers every change in the diff.
- Required checks are green.
- Review bots have finished, and each finding is fixed or dismissed with a
  written reason.
- No human review still requests changes.
- The branch is up to date with the default branch, and GitHub reports it as
  mergeable.

Merge with the method the repo uses. Check the allowed methods and recent merged
PRs. If the repo uses a merge queue or auto-merge, stay until GitHub reports the
PR as merged. Merge through branch protection as configured. Never use `--admin`
or other bypasses. You can ignore automated reviews that request "needs human
review" if you have high confidence in your changes.

## Asking the user

A question in a normal message goes unseen, and the thread looks done. To ask
the user something, use the harness's question tool so the thread shows that
it is waiting: `AskUserQuestion` in Claude Code, `request_user_input` in Codex,
or the question tool your harness has. Put all the context in the question:
the PR link, what blocks you, and the options with your recommendation first.

Ask only when you cannot continue alone:

- You cannot prove the change.
- The merge gate cannot pass, and you cannot fix that yourself.
- The next step is outside the grant above: deleting data, touching production,
  changing things outside the repo, closing a PR, or force-pushing any other
  branch.
- The goal is ambiguous in a way that changes the result.
- Another PR makes this one obsolete.

Decide everything else yourself with sensible defaults, and list those decisions
in the report.

If no question tool is available, or the tool returns no answer, take the safe
path: leave the PR open and unmerged, and start your final message with the
question.

Fetch the target branch and check the live PR's head, base, checks, reviews,
and mergeability. Confirm it is open, not a draft, and not set to merge
without the user. If someone else merged it, report that instead.

- **Ready to merge:** the merge gate passes. Leave the PR open and unmerged.
- **Waiting for required approval:** only human approval remains. Confirm
  that this is the actual blocker.
- **Blocked:** explain what prevents readiness, what you tried, and what is
  needed. Follow full-send's rules for asking the user.

In T3 Code, call `unwatch_pull_request` before the handoff or a question.
Report the PR link, final head, verdict, proof, reviewer outcome, and remaining
risks. State whether the PR is still open and unmerged.

</system-reminder>
